title: Orchestrated geo-fallback hypothesis and shed plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Design and implement an orchestrated multi-region routing policy that favors low-latency local endpoints while providing capacity-aware failover and progressive load-shedding. The goal is to keep customer-facing tail latency SLOs and availability targets during regional congestion or partial outages without manual intervention. Scope includes controller logic, region-level circuit-breakers, pinning heuristics, capacity-credit accounting, observability, and a canary rollout plan.

Background and motivation: We consistently see spikes where a single busy region causes global tail-latency regressions because traffic redistributes suboptimally or floods healthy regions. Current routing is simplistic: latency-first with hard geo pin fallthrough and global retries; this leads to overload and cascading degradation. We need a coordinated policy that understands regional capacity signals, respects SLOs, and enforces graceful degradation (user-prioritized shedding, degraded model variants, or queue shedding) before exhausting fallthrough targets.

SLO targets (for decisioning):
- Global read availability: 99.95% monthly
- Per-request p50/p95/p99 tail latency for interactive endpoints: 50ms / 120ms / 250ms (target)
- Degradation budget: keep fraction of requests served with degraded model < 2% under normal load, allow up to 10% during sustained regional failure windows

Design overview:
1) Latency-weighted primary selection: each request is scored by a latency affinity score computed from recent p95 observed+probe RTTs; prefer lowest score subject to capacity constraints.
2) Soft geo-pinning: maintain soft affinity tokens per user/customer (sticky by user-id/API token) with TTL. Soft pin respects capacity: when pinned region reports overload tokens, affinity becomes probabilistic with decaying weight; hard pin only applied in user-configured enterprise contracts.
3) Region circuit-breakers: region-level state machine (CLOSED, SOFT_OPEN, HARD_OPEN). Triggers: sustained p95 > threshold, GPU utilization > 90% for 30s, queue length > configured high-water mark. SOFT_OPEN enables progressive mitigation (shed low-priority traffic, route to degraded model), HARD_OPEN rejects or routes only to emergency fallback pool. Recovery via hysteresis and increasing probe checks.
4) Capacity credits & steering: each region maintains a credit balance computed from reserved capacity, recent throughput, and autoscaler headroom. The routing controller consults credits; when credits drop below thresholds, region receives a negative steering weight. Credits regenerated as autoscaler ramps or utilization lowers.
5) Progressive load-shedding ladder: a configurable policy that applies mitigations in order: prefix cache reuse, routing stopgap (redirect non-critical customers), degraded-quantized model, token-shed (rate-limit bursts), reject (last resort). We prioritize shedding by customer tier and by request latency sensitivity label.
6) Hedging and retry policy: client-side hedging for long tails up to one additional regional candidate. Retries respect idempotency and have backoff jitter. Hedging disabled for regions in HARD_OPEN.

Telemetry & signals required:
- region.p95_latency, region.cpu_util, region.gpu_util, region.queue_depth, region.inflight_tokens, region.queued_requests_by_priority
- per-model kv-cache hit rates and cache-size pressure metrics
- request-level routing_decision_trace for sampling (to reconstruct why a request was steered)
- derived signals: region_capacity_credits, region_slo_slack

Telemetry consumers and dashboards:
- New region routing dashboard (p95, credits, circuit-breaker state, shed rate)
- Alert rules: immediate paged alert when region enters HARD_OPEN and global availability drops below 99.9% for 2m; warning alerts for SOFT_OPEN and credits < 20%

API & config:
- Per-customer config: hard_pin_allowed (bool), priority_tier (0..3), prefer_locality (enum)
- Global routing config: soft_pin_ttl, credit_thresholds, circuit_breaker thresholds, shedding_ladder ordering

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for circuit-breaker state transitions and credit arithmetic
- Integration load tests in perf-staging with script that induces region saturation patterns (GPU burn, queue flood, intermittent packet loss)
- Canary rollout plan: 5% of traffic regionally for 72h with telemetry gating. Rollout gates: no increase in global p95 beyond 5% of baseline, no HARD_OPEN events, shed_rate under 2% for gold customers.

Operational runbook (short):
- If SOFT_OPEN: observe shed-rate and regional autoscaling; increase min capacity if persistent.
- If HARD_OPEN: disable routing to region except emergency pool, notify infra to investigate node health, escalate if not resolved in 15min.

Migration notes:
- Start with read-only interactive endpoints (text generation) and one test tenant group.
- Backfill historical telemetry to tune credit thresholds and latency scoring weights.

Open questions:
- How to integrate cross-region KV cache invalidation semantics with pinning? (Impact: heavy cache cold-starts)
- Tradeoffs on hedging aggressiveness for enterprise vs anonymous traffic
- Coordination with Dedicated cluster reservation logic (interaction with reserved capacity credits)

Deliverables: design doc, controller implementation, region circuit-breaker library, dashboards, e2e load test scripts, rollout checklist, PRD link (TBD).
